records.label: 16 patients from four families with Wolfram syndrome
records.segregation: Linkage to 4p16.1 excluded in three families, which showed linkage to 4q22-24; the two affected members of the fourth family were homozygous for 4p16.1 markers
quotes: To pursue the possibility of locus heterogeneity, 16 patients from four different families were recruited. These patients, who have the Wolfram syndrome phenotype, also have additional features that have not previously been reported.
There is an absence of diabetes insipidus in all affected family members. In addition, several patients have profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding.

records.label: Three consanguineous Jordanian families with Wolfram syndrome

phenotypes.text: increased thapsigargin-stimulated rise in intracellular calcium in lymphoblastoid cells

variants.consequence: missense; aberrant splicing with exon 2 skipping and premature stop codon

quotes: A single missense mutation was identified in a novel, highly conserved zinc-finger gene, ZCD2, in three consanguineous families of Jordanian descent with Wolfram syndrome (WFS).
A G-->C transversion at nucleotide 109 predicts an amino acid change from glutamic acid to glutamine (E37Q).

records.label: FS

phenotypes.text: absent platelet secretion in response to ADP

variants.as_reported: homozygous deletion affecting the whole exon 2 of CISD2

records.segregation: Homozygous in proband; parents and brother heterozygous carriers, clinically unaffected but with subclinical reversible ADP platelet aggregation defect
quotes: Since the age of 5 years old, FS suffered from recurrent b-UIU.
CISD2 cDNA sequencing revealed a novel homozygous deletion affecting the whole exon 2 of CISD2

Currently, FS is 22 years old and presents DM, ON with preserved visual acuity and electrophysiologic tests, no OA, tinnitus due to SHLHF triggered by loud environments, EGBR, slow intestinal transit, reduced and reversible defective PA to ADP, and b-UIU.

records.label: Italian siblings
quotes: Wolfram syndrome 2: a novel CISD2 mutation identified in Italian siblings.

notes.statement: Mozzillo et al. (2014) mapped the CISD2 exon 2 deletion by SNP array and PCR to a maximum of 2,050 bp; the deleted region included codons for amino acids 102 to 106 within the 2Fe-2S domain, which the authors suggested may result in a nonfunctional protein. Although the parents denied consanguinity and runs of homozygosity did not show a relationship, microsatellite analysis supported a common ancestor; the grandparents were born on the same small Italian island.
quotes: Thus, the maximum deletion size has been restricted to a region of 2,050 bp spanning from intron 2 to intron 3.

the triplets coding for aminoacids WRSKT, from the position 102 to 106 of the polypeptide, are within the deleted region, and this may result in a non functional protein because of zinc-finger domain lost.
Microsatellite analysis confirmed the hypothesis of a common ancestor (data not shown).

notes.statement: Mozzillo et al. (2014) noted that their patient had optic neuropathy rather than optic atrophy and impaired platelet aggregation to ADP rather than to collagen. They proposed that the ocular disease in the Jordanian patients may also have been optic neuropathy, and suggested that so-called WFS2 might not be a subtype of Wolfram syndrome.
quotes: Since our patient does not show OA at the age of 22 years, and since “asymptomatic” OA described in Jordanians is not completely supported, we suppose that the ocular pathology in those patients was probably ON and not OA.
the absence of OA, one of the main diagnostic criteria of WFS, suggests that the so-called WFS2 could not be a WFS subtype.

notes.statement: Mozzillo et al. (2014) found that the proband's heterozygous parents and brother had no ophthalmologic abnormalities, diabetes, or deafness, but did have a reversible ADP-induced platelet aggregation defect.
quotes: Ophtalmological abnormalities, DM and deafness were not found in the parents and brother, whereas a reversible PA in response to ADP was found.

notes.statement: Chen et al. (2009) found that Cisd2 deficiency in mice caused mitochondrial breakdown and dysfunction accompanied by autophagic cell death, preceding the earliest manifestations of nerve and muscle degeneration and leading to features suggestive of premature aging. Mitochondrial degeneration worsened with age, and autophagy increased in parallel with the premature aging phenotype.
quotes: Cisd2 deficiency in mice causes mitochondrial breakdown and dysfunction accompanied by autophagic cell death, and these events precede the two earliest manifestations of nerve and muscle degeneration; together, they lead to a panel of phenotypic features suggestive of premature aging.
mitochondrial degeneration exacerbates with age, and the autophagy increases in parallel to the development of the premature aging phenotype

notes.statement: Chen et al. (2009) found that Cisd2 localized mainly to mitochondria. On the basis of their knockout mouse findings, they proposed that WFS2 is a mitochondria-mediated disorder caused by CISD2 mutation, supporting the earlier clinical hypothesis that WFS is partly mitochondria-mediated.
quotes: Our study also reveals that Cisd2 is primarily localized in the mitochondria

our Cisd2 knockout mouse work provides strong evidence supporting an earlier clinical hypothesis that WFS is in part a mitochondria-mediated disorder; specifically, we propose that mutation of CISD2 causes the mitochondria-mediated disorder WFS2 in humans.

notes.statement: Amr et al. (2007) noted that the three Jordanian families with Wolfram syndrome did not have WFS1 mutations and had been mapped to the WFS2 locus at 4q22-q25.
quotes: It had been shown that these families did not have mutations in the WFS1 gene (WFS1) but were mapped to the WFS2 locus at 4q22-25.

notes.statement: Amr et al. (2007) found that the E37Q mutation in ZCD2, although nonsynonymous at a conserved residue, was pathogenic because it disrupted mRNA splicing, eliminating exon 2 and introducing a premature stop codon.
quotes: the pathogenesis for the disorder is because the mutation also causes aberrant splicing. The mutation was found to disrupt messenger RNA splicing by eliminating exon 2, and it results in the introduction of a premature stop codon.

notes.statement: Amr et al. (2007) did not identify mutations in the WFS2 gene in 377 probands with hearing loss.
quotes: Screening of 377 probands with hearing loss did not identify mutations in the WFS2 gene.

notes.statement: Amr et al. (2007) showed that the ZCD2-encoded protein, ERIS (endoplasmic reticulum intermembrane small protein), localized to the endoplasmic reticulum but did not interact directly with wolframin.
quotes: The ZCD2-encoded protein, ERIS (endoplasmic reticulum intermembrane small protein), is also shown to localize to the endoplasmic reticulum but does not interact directly with Wolframin.

notes.statement: Amr et al. (2007) found that lymphoblastoid cells from affected individuals showed a significantly greater rise in intracellular calcium on thapsigargin stimulation than controls, with no difference in resting intracellular calcium.
quotes: Lymphoblastoid cells from affected individuals show a significantly greater rise in intracellular calcium when stimulated with thapsigargin, compared with controls, although no difference was observed in resting concentrations of intracellular calcium.

notes.statement: El-Shanti et al. (2000) significantly excluded linkage to the chromosome 4p16.1 Wolfram syndrome locus in three of four families, using markers D4S432, D4S3023, and D4S2366. In these three families, they showed linkage to chromosome 4q22-24.
quotes: With the use of three microsatellite markers (D4S432, D4S3023, and D4S2366) reported to be linked to the chromosome 4p16.1 locus, we significantly excluded linkage in three of the four families.
For the other three families, genetic heterogeneity for Wolfram syndrome was verified by demonstration of linkage to chromosome 4q22-24.

notes.statement: El-Shanti et al. (2000) found that the two affected members of one family were homozygous for all three markers in the 4p16.1 region, while the other three families were linked to 4q22-24. The authors considered this further evidence for genetic heterogeneity in Wolfram syndrome.
quotes: The two affected individuals in one family showed homozygosity for all three markers from the region of linkage on chromosome 4p16.1.
provide further evidence for the genetic heterogeneity of this disorder

notes.statement: El-Shanti et al. (2000) reported that none of the affected members of the four families had diabetes insipidus. Several patients had profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding, which the authors described as features not previously reported in Wolfram syndrome.
quotes: There is an absence of diabetes insipidus in all affected family members. In addition, several patients have profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding.
